{{Short description|Theorem in mathematics}}
{{one source |date=March 2024}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Laplace's principle''' is a basic [[theorem]] in [[large deviations theory]] which is similar to [[Varadhan's lemma]]. It gives an [[Asymptotic analysis|asymptotic expression]] for the [[Lebesgue integration|Lebesgue integral]] of exp(&minus;''&theta;&phi;''(''x'')) over a fixed set ''A'' as ''&theta;'' becomes large. Such expressions can be used, for example, in [[statistical mechanics]] to determining the limiting behaviour of a system as the temperature tends to [[absolute zero]].

==Statement of the result==

Let ''A'' be a [[Lebesgue measure|Lebesgue-measurable]] [[subset]] of ''d''-[[dimension]]al [[Euclidean space]] '''R'''<sup>''d''</sup> and let ''&phi;''&nbsp;:&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''d''</sup>&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R''' be a [[measurable function]] with

:<math>\int_A e^{-\varphi(x)} \,dx < \infty.</math>

Then

:<math>\lim_{\theta \to \infty} \frac1{\theta} \log \int_A e^{-\theta \varphi(x)} \, dx = - \mathop{\mathrm{ess \, inf}}_{x \in A} \varphi(x),</math>

where ess&nbsp;inf denotes the [[essential infimum]]. Heuristically, this may be read as saying that for large ''&theta;'',

:<math>\int_A e^{-\theta \varphi(x)} \, dx \approx \exp \left(-\theta \mathop{\mathrm{ess \, inf}}_{x \in A} \varphi(x) \right).</math>

==Application==

The Laplace principle can be applied to the family of [[probability measure]]s '''P'''<sub>''&theta;''</sub> given by

:<math>\mathbf{P}_\theta (A) = \left( \int_A e^{-\theta \varphi(x)} \, dx \right) \bigg/ \left( \int_{\mathbf{R}^{d}} e^{-\theta \varphi(y)} \, dy \right)</math>

to give an asymptotic expression for the probability of some event ''A'' as ''&theta;'' becomes large. For example, if ''X'' is a standard [[normal distribution|normally distributed]] [[random variable]] on '''R''', then

:<math>\lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \varepsilon \log \mathbf{P} \big[ \sqrt{\varepsilon} X \in A \big] = - \mathop{\mathrm{ess \, inf}}_{x \in A} \frac{x^2}{2}</math>

for every measurable set ''A''.
